name: Odysseus
hook: Homer's wandering hero — Cyclops, Sirens, Circe and the long road back to Ithaca.

facts.label: Ithaca
facts.statement: Ithaca is his home island, where Penelope and son Telemachus wait; his father Laertes shares a name with Ophelia's brother.

facts.label: Penelope
facts.statement: Penelope stays faithful for 20 years and sets a contest: whoever strings Odysseus' great bow wins her.

facts.label: Polyphemus
facts.statement: Odysseus blinds Polyphemus, the Cyclops, after the one-eyed giant eats some of his men.

facts.label: Circe
facts.statement: Circe the enchantress keeps him a year; Calypso holds him seven years on the island of Ogygia.

facts.label: the Sirens
facts.statement: To hear the Sirens without dying, Odysseus has himself tied to the mast as the ship sails past.

facts.label: Athena
facts.statement: Athena, goddess of wisdom, aids Odysseus in disguise and pleads with Zeus to free him from Calypso.

facts.label: Ulysses (the novel)
facts.statement: James Joyce's 1922 novel Ulysses recasts him as Dubliner Leopold Bloom and ends with Molly Bloom's long monologue.
